thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — after the 2am runtime merge I’m seeing a regression on A100 for long sequences (seqlen > 1024). p99 latency up ~12% on our a3-longseq job.

devin: Ugh. Any idea which change caused it? :eyes:

maria: Looks like the new kernel gating change. The selector started preferring the small-tile, warp-specialized kernel for seqlen around 800–1400. On A100 that path increases register pressure and causes occasional spills when the batch has heterogenous lengths.

dani: Can you paste the exact selector config that triggered it?

maria: Sure — local copy of the applied override: ```yaml
kernel_selector:
  mode: gated
  gating_threshold: 768    # previously 1536
  prefer_small_tile: true
  small_tile: 128
  fallback_tile: 256
  prefetch_kv: bank_aware
```

maria: Also attaching a tiny profiler snippet: ```
# trimmed p99 wall times (ms)
seqlen 512  -> 18.2
seqlen 1024 -> 25.6
seqlen 1536 -> 39.4 (was 35.1 pre-change)
# register spill counters jumped ~22% on the small-tile kernel for seqlen 1536
```

perf-bot: @maria uploaded perf trace: https://perf.internal/trace/1988881234 (cpu/gpu timelines + nvprof counters)

devin: So gating threshold was lowered and that made the selector choose the wrong kernel for mid-long sequences. Two levers: 1) raise gating_threshold back to 1536, 2) teach selector to incorporate estimated register usage per tile.

dani: Agree. Also note KV cache behavior: when register pressure spikes we observed more frequent KV eviction on the fast-path because the warp-specialized kernel used more shared memories for prefetch windows; that increases memory pressure and causes the CPU-side eviction policy to trigger earlier.

rao: If KV evictions are upstream, batch packing might amplify it. Mixed-length batches with a few long requests push those kernels into the batch and cause cross-contamination. We should try conservative batching for now (max_total_tokens cap) to reduce heterogeneity.

maria: Plan I propose: revert gating_threshold -> 1536 in prod (canary 10%), add a selector metric to simulate register usage and add it to autotuner scoring, and patch the batching heuristic to enforce a 20% length-homogeneity rule for long-seq routes.

devin: Sounds good. Can we also add a quick perf test to CI that runs seqlen=1536 on an A100 smoke job? Make it non-blocking but surface as a perf alert.

maria: Yep — will open PR for revert + CI trace.

dani: For the autotuner change: we should model tile->reg pressure as a linear estimator first, e.g. reg_est = base_reg + reg_per_token * tile_size. Then score = latency + alpha * reg_est. Alpha tuned from profiling.

rao: I can own the autotuner PR. Will add the reg estimator and a calibration job to fit alpha.

infra-bot: Canary rollout initiated for config revert (10% of hosts). ID: canary-1988881234. Watch perf dashboard: https://dash.internal/prod/rls/1988

maria: Thanks all. If the canary looks good over the next 30m we can push full revert, and merge the autotuner change later this week.

devin: :thumbsup: Also leave a short note in the release checklist so we don't flip gating_threshold without perf parens next time.

maria: Will do.
